open_points.subject: M23 NodeExecution identity
open_points.text: Identity: value; Identity evidence: “an attempt's record is issued once”
open_points.question: Is a NodeExecution a value record or an entity/observation, and what is its identity?
options: Treat it as an entity identified by run_id, node_id, map_index and attempt_number
Treat it as a content-derived value
Add a separately minted NodeExecution identity
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an entity identified by its run, node, element and attempt tuple.

open_points.subject: File-port value_schema
open_points.text: “Every port carries a value schema”; “the kernel does not inspect file content”; “a file port carries bytes”
open_points.question: What does value_schema constrain on a file port, and what does it mean for a file fixture or file value to fit that schema?
options: Use the schema only as an exact wiring label and validate file values only as bytes
Validate metadata such as digest and size against the schema
Validate the file content against the schema
open_points.default_guess: Use it only as a wiring label; validate bytes, media type and size separately.

open_points.subject: Flow input and output schemas
open_points.text: Composition refuses specified malformed flow properties, but does not say that a flow input or output value_schema must be within the supported schema subset.
open_points.question: May a flow version declare an unsupported schema, and if not, is that refused before the version is kept or returned as a proof failure?
options: Refuse composition before keeping the version
Keep the version and fail its proof
Allow any schema on flow ports
open_points.default_guess: Refuse composition before keeping the version.

open_points.subject: FlowConstant declared schema
open_points.text: “a constant whose value does not fit the schema declared with it”
open_points.question: What happens when a constant's declared schema is malformed or outside the supported schema subset, given that the kernel must validate the value against it before keeping the version?
options: Refuse composition as malformed before keeping the version
Keep it and fail proof phase 2
Attempt validation using schemas outside the supported subset
open_points.default_guess: Refuse composition before keeping the version.

open_points.subject: FlowVersion content identity ordering
open_points.text: “edges in the edge order of A05, constants by (to_node, to_port)”
open_points.question: How are identity lists ordered when those sort keys tie, such as legal edges with the same endpoints but different guard values or duplicate constants aimed at one port?
options: Add a canonical tie-breaker using the complete canonical item
Preserve submission order for tied items
Refuse every tied key before computing identity
open_points.default_guess: Use the complete canonical item as a deterministic tie-breaker.

open_points.subject: Empty node identifiers
open_points.text: “A flow input or flow output endpoint has the empty string as its node”; node_id is only said to be unique within the version.
open_points.question: Is an empty node_id allowed, and if so how is it distinguished and ordered against a flow endpoint?
options: Refuse an empty node_id at composition
Allow it but tag endpoint kinds separately in every identity and order
Treat it as the same ordering key as a flow endpoint
open_points.default_guess: Refuse an empty node_id.

open_points.subject: Sandbox filesystem access
open_points.text: K-02 says “no filesystem beyond its input”; A03 permits opening paths inside “the exchange directory and the read-only runtime.”
open_points.question: May agent code read or write arbitrary paths inside the exchange directory and read arbitrary runtime files, or only use the input and output objects supplied by the runner?
options: Permit general exchange-directory scratch and runtime reads
Expose only runner-managed input and output files
Prohibit all direct filesystem access by agent code
open_points.default_guess: Expose only runner-managed inputs and outputs and reject other direct file access.

open_points.subject: Sandbox clock prohibition
open_points.text: “Functions have no clock”; “The replaced entry points are exactly” the listed functions.
open_points.question: Does the closed trap list take precedence even though CPython 3.12 exposes other timing sources such as thread_time, clock_gettime, os.times and resource usage, or must every usable clock source be blocked?
options: Block every clock source, expanding the release list
Block only the enumerated entry points
Permit deterministic or CPU-time clocks but not wall time
open_points.default_guess: Block every usable clock source and make the complete release list match that rule.

open_points.subject: Sandbox audit traps
open_points.text: “installs an audit hook that raises on socket, subprocess, ctypes and on opening any path outside”
open_points.question: Which exact CPython audit events and operations count as socket, subprocess, ctypes and file-opening violations, including os.fork, Unix sockets, dynamic loading and descriptor-based file access?
options: Define a closed release-specific audit-event and operation list
Treat any related CPython audit event as a violation
Rely only on bubblewrap and classify traps opportunistically
open_points.default_guess: Define and test a closed release-specific list covering every prohibited operation.

open_points.subject: Function determinism
open_points.text: “Admission is a deterministic verdict”; required test: “The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.”
open_points.question: How is determinism guaranteed or refused for arbitrary standard-library Python that can use thread scheduling, process scheduling, object identities and other nondeterministic observations not trapped by A03?
options: Enforce a stronger sandbox that removes all such observations
Run repeated trials and refuse inconsistent implementations
Define determinism only as deterministic processing of the observations produced by one admission run
open_points.default_guess: Refuse implementations whose repeated executions on the same cases produce different outcomes or output digests.

open_points.subject: Release dependency pinning
open_points.text: “one release fixes every ceiling and every dependency”; “the sandbox interpreter of release v1 is CPython 3.12”; the only bubblewrap start check is that it is present and a probe succeeds.
open_points.question: Which exact CPython patch version and bubblewrap version are part of release v1, and must startup refuse other versions?
options: Pin and verify exact CPython and bubblewrap versions
Accept any CPython 3.12 patch and any bubblewrap passing the probe
Treat host bubblewrap as outside the release dependency invariant
open_points.default_guess: Pin and verify exact compatible versions.

open_points.subject: Sandbox resource outcomes
open_points.text: “a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, output_bytes) — resource_exhausted”
open_points.question: What observable evidence constitutes a limit hit when the OS reports an allocation or fork failure, the program catches that failure, the process is killed, or a timeout and limit event occur at nearly the same time?
options: Classify from parent-observed counters and limit signals even if user code catches an error
Classify as resource_exhausted only when the supervisor terminates the process
Let a caught limit error produce the program's eventual outcome
open_points.default_guess: Use parent-observed limit evidence, with timeout taking precedence exactly as listed.

open_points.subject: Installation token format
open_points.text: “any token shorter than 43 characters (32 bytes in base64url)”
open_points.question: Must tokens be valid unpadded base64url decoding to at least 32 bytes, or is a length of 43 arbitrary characters sufficient?
options: Require valid unpadded base64url representing at least 32 bytes
Check only character length
Require exactly 43 base64url characters
open_points.default_guess: Require valid unpadded base64url representing at least 32 bytes.

open_points.subject: Data-directory privacy
open_points.text: “The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.”
open_points.question: Which owners, permission bits, ACLs and directory traversal permissions satisfy “private,” and is the check recursive over all existing entries?
options: Require kernel-user ownership and no group/other permissions recursively
Check only the data directory and files opened by the kernel
Accept ACL-based equivalent privacy
open_points.default_guess: Require kernel-user ownership and no group/other permissions on the directory and every existing entry.

open_points.subject: Startup checks and recovery
open_points.text: A03 checks the sandbox “before recovery and before the surface opens”; A14 performs recovery on start; A17 and A18 independently define configuration, lock, permission, symlink and cleanup checks.
open_points.question: What is the deterministic order of all startup checks, temporary/spool cleanup, in-flight conversion and run advancement, and which failure is reported when several fail?
options: Specify one global ordered startup sequence
Run independent checks in implementation-defined order
Report all startup failures without a first one
open_points.default_guess: Acquire and validate configuration and storage first, validate the sandbox next, clean temporary files, then recover and advance runs before opening the surface.

open_points.subject: Manifest revision access
open_points.text: “reads a service's record only from <manifest_location>/<service_id>.json at the configured manifest_revision”
open_points.question: How is a file read “at” manifest_revision without changing the working tree, and what is refused when the location is not a repository or the revision cannot be resolved?
options: Read the file directly from the named VCS revision object
Require manifest_location already to be an immutable checkout of that revision
Ignore manifest_revision and read the current filesystem file
open_points.default_guess: Read the file from the named revision object and refuse an unresolved location or revision.

open_points.subject: Manifest document shape
open_points.text: Rule 5 covers a record that “is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities” but does not define the required JSON types or treatment of malformed, duplicate-key or incomplete capability and instance objects.
open_points.question: What complete manifest shape is accepted, and does malformed data in an unrelated capability or instance invalidate the record or only the selected operation and instance?
options: Validate the whole service record against one closed manifest schema
Validate only fields needed for the selected operation and instance
Ignore malformed unrelated entries except duplicate operation names
open_points.default_guess: Validate the whole relevant service record against a closed manifest schema.

open_points.subject: Credential-header startup check
open_points.text: “an installation whose credential header has ... the name of a required header ... refuses to start”; manifest operations are otherwise read on demand.
open_points.question: At startup, which manifest instance records are read for this collision check, and what happens if one is absent, malformed or cannot be read?
options: Read every selected instance and refuse startup on any unreadable or malformed record
Check only services with configured credentials and defer other manifest failures
Perform no startup collision check until an invocation
open_points.default_guess: Read every selected service instance needed by configured credentials and refuse startup if the collision check cannot be completed.

open_points.subject: api_base_url composition
open_points.text: “api_base_url” need only be “an absolute http or https URL with a host”; the request URL is “the api_base_url without a trailing / followed by the declared path.”
open_points.question: Are user information, query, fragment, percent-encoded path separators and non-root base paths allowed in api_base_url, and precisely how are trailing slashes removed and the path joined?
options: Restrict base URLs to scheme, authority and an optional normalized path with no query, fragment or user information
Allow all absolute URLs and concatenate their serialized text
Use standard URL resolution semantics
open_points.default_guess: Reject user information, query and fragment, preserve an optional base path, remove all trailing slashes from that path and append the declared path literally.

open_points.subject: Plain-HTTP loopback exception
open_points.text: “or one whose api_base_url host is a loopback address”
open_points.question: What counts as a loopback host: only literal IPv4 and IPv6 loopback addresses, or also names that resolve to loopback, and when is resolution checked?
options: Allow only literal loopback IP addresses
Resolve the hostname and allow it only when every address is loopback
Allow common names such as localhost
open_points.default_guess: Allow only literal loopback IPv4 or IPv6 addresses.

open_points.subject: Multipart port names
open_points.text: “Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"”, with filename="<port>" added for a file part”
open_points.question: What happens when a port name contains a quote, backslash, control character, non-ASCII text or another character requiring Content-Disposition escaping?
options: Restrict multipart-used port names to a safe ASCII token syntax
Define an exact escaping and encoding algorithm
Insert the port name verbatim
open_points.default_guess: Refuse bindings whose multipart port names are not safe ASCII field names.

open_points.subject: HTTP timeout after a status is received
open_points.text: “request may have been sent, no valid final response received (timeout...)”; separately, “status 4xx, whatever the body's size” is not_applied.
open_points.question: If a final 4xx, 3xx, 5xx or 2xx status and headers arrive but the body stalls, resets or times out, does the status row decide the outcome or is there no valid final response?
options: A final status decides the status-class outcome even if its body does not complete
The response is valid only after the required body has completed, so the no-valid-response row wins
Status decides only for responses whose bodies are deliberately ignored
open_points.default_guess: Treat the response as invalid until its required body handling completes; for a non-read operation the outcome is unknown.

open_points.subject: HTTP transport deadline
open_points.text: “it arrived within transport_timeout_ms”
open_points.question: From what event to what event is transport_timeout_ms measured, and is it one total deadline or separate DNS, connect, write, header and body deadlines?
options: One monotonic deadline from invocation start through the complete handled response body
A deadline beginning when the first request byte is written
Separate timeout budgets for transport phases
open_points.default_guess: Use one monotonic deadline from invocation start through completion of the handled response.

open_points.subject: Mapped aggregate value failure trace
open_points.text: “a list whose canonical bytes exceed stored_value_bytes_max ... fails the node”; “No record of the node states that failure ... the same way by every reader of the trace.”
open_points.question: How is the mapped node's derived failure and reason exposed and verified, especially for an agent that cannot receive personal-data values or identifiers needed to recompute the list?
options: Have inspection compute and return a defined derived node status and reason
Write an immutable aggregate NodeExecution for the mapped node
Expose only failed dependants and the failed run, without a node-level reason
open_points.default_guess: Have the kernel return a defined derived status and value_too_large reason while keeping element records immutable.

open_points.subject: Ordering of derived skip and upstream-failure records
open_points.text: “The next node is the ready node with the smallest node_id”; “Records of nodes that become non-executable together are written in (node_id, map_index) order.”
open_points.question: When some nodes are ready to execute while other nodes have just become skipped_by_guard or upstream_failed, are all derived terminal records written before selecting the next ready node, after it, or interleaved by node_id?
options: Close all currently derivable skipped and upstream-failed nodes before executing another node
Execute the smallest ready node first
Choose the smallest node_id across executable and derivably terminal nodes
open_points.default_guess: Choose the smallest node_id across both executable and derivably terminal nodes, applying the stated status precedence.

open_points.subject: Unnamed spool-file replacement
open_points.text: “after any other failure they stay in the run's spool unnamed ... or a later write to the same position replaces them”; SpooledFile identity includes attempt_number.
open_points.question: What is a spool “position” for an unnamed failed-attempt file, and can a later attempt with a different attempt_number ever write that same position?
options: Position excludes attempt_number, so a later attempt replaces the prior unnamed file for the same node, element, port and list index
Position includes attempt_number, so later attempts never replace it
Delete all unnamed files at the end of each failed attempt
open_points.default_guess: Use node, element, port and list index as the replaceable position, while recorded successful files retain attempt-specific immutable names.

open_points.subject: Kernel timestamp event points
open_points.text: “Every timestamp the kernel records comes from one clock module”
open_points.question: At which exact event is each requested_at, started_at, ended_at, recorded_at, concluded_at, activated_at and similar timestamp sampled, and do fields written in one transaction share one reading or use separate readings?
options: Define an event point for every timestamp and share a transaction/event reading where applicable
Read the clock independently when each field is serialized
Use one timestamp for the entire surface request
open_points.default_guess: Define each timestamp at its named state transition and use one clock reading for fields created by the same atomic transition.

open_points.subject: Filtered list pagination
open_points.text: “The continuation token is the store position of the last item returned; the next page starts below it.”
open_points.question: What continuation token is returned when a filtered page finds no matching item before reaching the scan limit but older records may still match, and does page_size limit matched items or records scanned?
options: Page size counts matching items and scanning continues until that many are found or the record type is exhausted
Page size counts scanned records and an empty page may carry a scan-position token
An empty page always means there are no later matches
open_points.default_guess: Count matching items and continue scanning until the page is full or the record type is exhausted.

open_points.subject: Redacted failure-detail length
open_points.text: “returned to an agent only as its length and that class”
open_points.question: Is failure-detail length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode scalar values or characters after replacement and truncation?
options: UTF-8 byte length of the stored bounded detail
Unicode scalar-value count
Source body byte length before decoding and truncation
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the stored bounded failure detail.
